purpose: Plan Batch 41 as the missing product-level first-run orchestration layer for Product-Agent OS.

analysis_summary.short_answer: Yes, the desired first-launch behavior is the product behavior that should exist. The earlier Batch 39 work built packet, renderer, graph, question, guardrail and hardening contracts, but did not assemble them into one end-user first-run automation command.
why_not_implemented_before: Previous work was sliced around safety and evidence contracts, not around a single product entrypoint.
The first-run packet and HTML renderer were intentionally implemented separately so generated views stayed orientation-only and could not become source truth.
Guided question primitives exist in discovery/question_protocol, but the first-run CLI does not call them as a first-launch UX.
Real-target evidence for Neural_Flow and SOL 0.6 arrived late in Batch 39 and exposed that the pieces were composable but not yet orchestrated.
Source-policy blockers and no-target-mutation rules made silent in-project artifact creation unsafe as a default.
B39-S4 and B39-S5 converted missing runtime/browser/public-site/live evidence into explicit blockers instead of hiding them behind a readiness claim.

current_evidence.fact: Batch 39 is closed for owner-feedback testing, not release readiness.
B39-FRIA-M20.1..M20.10 covered packet schema, CLI boundary, adapter, offline renderer, guardrails and scorecard policy, while explicitly not proving full first-run automation readiness.
B39-TEST-M21 rendered 11 generated first-run pages in a temporary copy and treated real-target output as inspection-only usefulness evidence.
B39-S5 decision records release/distribution=no_go, owner_feedback=conditional_go and runtime/browser=approval_required.
The current CLI accepts --dry-run or --write only. It has no no-args onboarding, --full-dry-run, --stage or --render-html mode.
The current first-run packet is composed from workspace inventory and marks runtime, graph and deeper checks as not_run or not_available.
The renderer can write the offline HTML artifact and manifest, but it is not wired into the first-run CLI.
The typed question_queue can expose only one blocking first-response question, but first-run automation does not yet surface it.

missing_from_original_prompt: Installed plugin/cache refresh readiness so the new command is available outside the source tree.
Privacy/redaction checks for generated HTML and JSON.
Explicit target write modes: read-only, stage and write-in-target-after-approval.
Cleanup and rollback for generated artifacts.
Deterministic synthetic fixture plus read-only Neural_Flow and SOL 0.6 pilots.
Answer-ledger routing so user answers become reviewed context or accepted gaps instead of hidden chat-only state.

first_run_should: Show help or guided intake when launched without enough arguments.
Run all safe read-only first-run checks by default.
Refuse or stage actions that would mutate the target without exact approval.
Detect project type, lifecycle state, stack, parameters, documentation system, logging system, source policy, methodologies and risks.
Build a merged first-run packet from discovery, source policy, methodology, graph, status, dependency readiness and runtime/browser boundary checks.
Render a complete offline HTML artifact with all first-run pages and manifest.
Compare with previous first-run manifest when present.
Ask one blocking question when owner input is required before the next safe step.
Preserve generated artifacts as orientation evidence only.
Print a concise summary of what was done, what was blocked, where the artifact is and what question needs an answer.
product_definition.batch41_done_when: A single first-run command can produce the merged packet, guided first response and offline HTML artifact in read-only or explicit stage mode, with target mutation proof and real-target read-only evidence for Neural_Flow and SOL 0.6.

html_cockpit_target.legacy_artifact_policy: existing 11-page first-run output is diagnostic/raw evidence only and must not be the primary end-user report
html_cockpit_target.source_of_truth_policy: generated cockpit, generated graph and generated diagnostics are orientation evidence only; source files and current command evidence remain source truth

large_graph_rendering.default_strategy: do not render 5000 nodes / 50000 edges in full by default; render clustered overview, sampled/aggregated edges, selected-neighborhood subgraphs, query-driven expansion and table fallback
large_graph_rendering.primary_renderer: locally bundled Cosmos.gl WebGL/GPU force graph renderer for the cockpit graph canvas and large-project exploration
large_graph_rendering.data_adapter: convert Product-Agent OS graph packets to Cosmos.gl typed arrays and index maps while preserving source-free metadata labels
large_graph_rendering.compatibility_adapter: Graphology-compatible payload remains the internal graph/query interchange format; Cosmos.gl is the selected visualization layer
large_graph_rendering.secondary_renderer: Sigma.js is kept only as a compatibility or fallback evaluation path, not the selected primary renderer
large_graph_rendering.non_primary_renderer: Cytoscape.js may be evaluated for smaller analysis/compound subgraphs but is not the primary renderer for 50000-edge cockpit views
large_graph_rendering.fallback_renderer: static SVG/Canvas summary, cluster cards and bounded table fallback when WebGL/vendor assets are unavailable
large_graph_rendering.dependency_policy: no CDN, no network fetch, no install by default; any vendored library requires version, license, hash and offline validation evidence
performance_gates: 1k graph fixture uses Cosmos.gl interactive mode within visible budget
5k graph fixture uses Cosmos.gl clustered overview, hidden labels, selected-neighborhood expansion and edge sampling
10k+ graph fixture or synthetic stress case stays responsive through Cosmos.gl LOD, hard visible limits and fallback table
50k-edge dense case validates link sampling, label suppression, fallback state and no browser-freeze regression
all graph modes preserve generated-view-only wording and do not imply source-read completeness
